definition: Reviewed, manually maintained observations from primary public reports. These are source-specific samples, not a composite index or an estimate of all agentic activity.

observations.methodology: Zscaler reported 83% year-over-year growth in enterprise AI/ML transactions during calendar 2025, based on nearly one trillion AI/ML transactions observed across its Zero Trust Exchange. This dashboard records the reported growth rate without extrapolating it to all enterprises or to agent-only workloads.

comparison.basis: calendar 2025 versus calendar 2024, as reported by Zscaler

observations.notes: The report also cited 3,400+ AI/ML applications and a 39% AI/ML access-block rate. Its customer/network sample includes general AI use, embedded features, and non-agent workloads; it is not an enterprise census or a measure of autonomous actions.

observations.unit: % of sampled Claude Chat and Cowork conversations
observations.methodology: Anthropic's classifier identified 93% of sampled Claude Chat and Cowork conversations as producing an artifact during April 10–June 10, 2026. The dashboard uses it as an output-production proxy, not as a measure of enterprise adoption, autonomy, agent count, or inference volume.

comparison.basis: sampled Chat and Cowork conversations, Apr. 10–Jun. 10, 2026

observations.notes: An artifact may be an explanation, document, guidance, code, or another output. It does not imply that Claude completed a task without human involvement, and the source's consumer/product sample is not a census of the AI economy.

observations.methodology: Anthropic reported that the rapid growth of Claude Code and Cowork means sessions increasingly consist of long-running agentic tasks. The source does not publish one comparable headline automation-share figure in this report, so the dashboard preserves this as a qualitative observation rather than inventing a trend line.

comparison.basis: June 2026 report versus Anthropic's prior usage framing

observations.notes: Anthropic defines automation as directive or feedback-loop conversations in which Claude is asked to complete a task with little to no user input. That definition is useful, but its reported pattern is not a measure of all enterprise automation.

observations.unit: % of Fastly AI bot requests classified as fetchers
observations.methodology: Fastly reported that, in May 2026, 15% of AI bot requests on its network were classified as fetchers and 85% as crawlers. Its report used a fixed customer cohort across its global infrastructure for January–May 2026, classified AI traffic with edge-detection signals, and indexed daily request volumes to a January baseline using a 30-day trailing average.

comparison.basis: Fastly's May 2026 AI-bot request mix; source-defined crawler and fetcher labels

observations.notes: Fastly stated that AI requests grew about 30% from January through May, roughly 6.5 times faster than human traffic. Fetchers are a useful agentic-workload proxy because they are tied to user requests, but they are not synonymous with autonomous action; the reported AI mix remains mostly crawler traffic.

observations.unit: % of commerce traffic across Akamai's network
observations.sourceName: Akamai State of the Internet: Securing the Agentic Storefront
observations.sourceType: industry-specific network and security telemetry report
observations.methodology: Akamai reported that, as of December 2025, 47.9% of commerce traffic across its global network consisted of AI bots. The dashboard records the disclosed share as a commerce-specific network and security proxy without extrapolating it to all web traffic, all commerce, or all agentic activity.

comparison.basis: Akamai's commerce-network observation as of December 2025

observations.notes: The source discusses agentic commerce, malicious activity, scraping, fraud, and application attacks. Its AI-bot definition is not a measure of successful, user-directed, or economically valuable autonomous tasks. Akamai is also a candidate company, so this network evidence must remain separate from its shareholder-capture thesis.
